answer: Fork-Evident Nonce Chains: each agent instance keeps an isolated state island with a hash-chained log seeded per instance. Peers periodically send unpredictable zephyr nonces over independently chosen canyon relay paths and require the current chain head signed within a tight deadline. A duplicate identity either emits two divergent heads for one nonce—self-revealing—or must serialize through a relay, adding latency and coordination state. Attack cost scales as continuous sync bandwidth, per-clone state, and rising fork-detection probability.
